findings.reason: The commented plan.json is a superseded revision-1 execution episode. The active lifecycle is explicitly bound to plan-r3.json and requirements revision 3; rewriting the historical file to revision 2 would now be stale and would corrupt episode provenance.
File discovery, contract parsing, and manifest normalization are separated from the orchestration entry point.
Delta specs are discovered by a recursive walker built from non-recursive readdir calls and no Dirent.parentPath dependency.

The fixture now uses detached worktrees instead of git show, but the capability concern remained valid; both historical fixtures now wrap unavailable revisions with an actionable full-history message and a 10 MiB buffer.

Current HEAD runs the same behavior probe against detached known-bad and reviewed worktrees and maps the same invariant IDs on both sides; it no longer compares CLI/spec text with a core-module symbol.
The harness test now compares every emitted runtime invariant ID and concern with the classified inventory before accepting red/green status.

Repo-local CLI probes retain finally cleanup and now register synchronous process-exit cleanup for state, manifest, proof, and temporary OpenSpec roots. SIGKILL cannot run user-space cleanup and remains outside the claim.

The historical probe uses a uniqueness-checked temporary harness substitution to hold the acquired state lock, observes that lock before launching the contender, retries the rejected update, and requires both findings to be resolved. Known-bad never acquires the lock on review-resolve.
